timeline.event: Master Services Agreement executed between Vantage and Coastal
Statement of Work #2 executed, expanding fulfillment volume 3x
Ashby internal email: 'we are already over capacity at the Norfolk facility, we should flag this before SOW 2 volume hits'
Coastal certificate of insurance delivered to Vantage, representing full coverage limits in effect
Fire at Coastal's Norfolk warehouse damages inventory awaiting fulfillment
Coastal issues formal force majeure notice to Vantage, citing the fire as an unforeseeable event excusing performance
Merrow Retail Group sends demand letter to Vantage over delayed shipments traced to the Coastal facility

evidence_map.description: Section 9 indemnification clause — Coastal to indemnify Vantage for third-party claims arising from Coastal's performance
Section 11 limitation of liability — caps Coastal's aggregate liability at 12 months' fees paid, with carve-out for indemnification obligations
Ashby email acknowledging capacity shortfall three weeks before the fire and before SOW 2 volume increase took effect
Coastal's force majeure notice characterizing the fire as the sole cause of nonperformance
Certificate of insurance representing coverage limits that do not match the policy Coastal actually held at the time of the fire

findings.title: Force majeure notice omits known pre-existing capacity shortfall
findings.description: Coastal's force majeure notice attributes nonperformance solely to the fire, but an internal email three weeks earlier shows Coastal already knew it was over capacity independent of the fire.
findings.source_quote: an unforeseeable event beyond Coastal's reasonable control

findings.title: Internal email contradicts force majeure causation theory
findings.description: See f-1. Ashby's internal email is the source of the contradiction.
findings.source_quote: we are already over capacity at the Norfolk facility

findings.title: Missing Coastal capacity-planning records for SOW 2 onboarding
findings.description: No production yet of Coastal's internal capacity assessments or staffing plans covering the period between SOW 2 execution and the fire.
findings.source_quote: we should flag this before SOW 2 volume hits

findings.title: Discrepancy between represented and actual insurance coverage
findings.description: The certificate of insurance Coastal delivered appears inconsistent with its actual policy limits at the time of loss; underlying policy documents have not been produced.

findings.title: Motion for partial summary judgment defeating the force majeure defense
findings.description: Internal email evidence that the shortfall predated and was independent of the fire supports defeating force majeure as a matter of law on the causation element.

findings.title: Limitation-of-liability cap may not reach the indemnification claim
findings.description: Section 11's carve-out for indemnification obligations means Coastal's liability cap likely does not shield it from the Merrow third-party claim routed through Section 9.

findings.title: Third-party indemnification exposure from Merrow demand letter
findings.description: The Merrow demand letter creates a live indemnification trigger under Section 9 that should be tendered to Coastal promptly to preserve the claim and any related insurance rights.
findings.source_quote: delayed shipments traced to the Coastal facility

findings.title: Known-shortfall theory defeats force majeure and supports breach
findings.description: The combination of the pre-fire capacity email and the subsequent force majeure notice supports a theory that Coastal's nonperformance was a foreseeable, self-inflicted breach rather than an excused event.
findings.source_quote: we should flag this before SOW 2 volume hits

contradictions.description: Coastal's force majeure notice is contradicted by its own internal email acknowledging a pre-existing, non-fire-related capacity shortfall.

discovery_gaps.description: Coastal capacity-planning and staffing records for the SOW 2 onboarding period not produced.
Underlying insurance policy documents to verify the certificate of insurance's represented limits.

motions.title: Motion for Partial Summary Judgment defeating force majeure defense
motions.basis: Internal email establishes the shortfall predated and was independent of the fire, defeating causation.

risks.description: Limitation-of-liability cap likely does not reach the indemnification carve-out for the Merrow third-party claim.
Certificate of insurance may misrepresent actual coverage in effect at time of loss.

theories.label: Known pre-existing shortfall defeats force majeure
